title: Michelin-Selected KEK Brings Singapore's Zi Char Cuisine to Bengaluru
excerpt: Keng Eng Kee Seafood, the 1970s-born zi char institution now run by three siblings, carries its wok hei and Michelin recognition to one of India's most adventurous food cities.
body:
• KEK — Keng Eng Kee Seafood, the Michelin-selected Singapore zi char restaurant — is bringing its cuisine to Bengaluru, The Hindu reports.
  • Born in the 1970s as a humble hawker stall founded by Hainanese grandparents, KEK is now run by third-generation siblings Paul, Wayne and Jiamin Liew.
  • Signature dishes include Moonlight Hor Fun, Coffee Pork Ribs, White Pepper Crab and Claypot Pig's Liver; the restaurant has held the Michelin Guide's Michelin Plate for seven years and been featured on Netflix and CNN.
  • Zi char (煮炒, "cook and fry") is Singapore's beloved home-style, cook-to-order cuisine — built for loud, communal feasting with family and friends.

Singapore's zi char cuisine is heading to Bengaluru. The Hindu reports that KEK — Keng Eng Kee Seafood, the Michelin-selected institution that turned a 1970s hawker stall into one of Singapore's most decorated family restaurants — is bringing its distinctive brand of home-style cooking to one of India's most adventurous food cities.

What Is Zi Char?

Zi char — written 煮炒 and pronounced "tze char" in Hokkien — translates roughly as "cook and fry." It describes the sprawling, cook-to-order home-style cuisine served at Singapore's coffee shops and hawker centres: dozens of wok-fired dishes made on demand, from seafood and meats to vegetables and rice, designed for sharing across a table with beer and conversation. For Singaporeans, a zi char joint is where birthdays, office wins and ordinary Fridays all get celebrated — the food is the excuse, the gathering is the point.

KEK is among the cuisine's most celebrated names. The restaurant began in the 1970s as a modest hawker stall run by grandparents who carried their cooking traditions from Hainan. Three generations on, siblings Paul, Wayne and Jiamin Liew run the operation from its home base at Alexandra Village in Bukit Merah, where queues of tourists and regulars alike line up for dishes that have become Singaporean legends.

The Dishes to Expect

KEK's menu is built on two pillars: wok hei — the smoky "breath of the wok" that defines great stir-fry — and original creations you will not find at other zi char joints. The signature Moonlight Hor Fun is flat rice noodles wok-tossed in dark soy sauce and crowned with a raw egg, mixed tableside for richness. Coffee Pork Ribs — the dish behind KEK's collaboration with Shake Shack — coats tender ribs in a bittersweet glaze made from coffee, apple jam and tomato sauce. White Pepper Crab is exactly what it sounds like, and the aromatic pepper sauce has earned its own following. Then there is the Claypot Pig's Liver, still sizzling with ginger and scallion when it lands on the table, and the Mingzhu Roll, a beancurd-skin parcel stuffed with salted egg yolk, mushrooms, ham and prawn, fried golden.

The pedigree is formidable: the Michelin Guide has awarded KEK its Michelin Plate for seven consecutive years, the restaurant has been featured on Netflix and CNN, and its flavours were deemed worthy of a full Shake Shack collaboration menu in Singapore. This is not fine dining — it is hawker craft at the highest level it has ever been recognized.

"What will remain the same is our respect for our heritage and our love for coming together around the table to have a good time."

— Paul Liew, KEK Seafood

Why Bengaluru

Bengaluru is arguably India's most natural home for an experiment like this. The city's dining scene has long rewarded the unfamiliar — from Japanese omakase counters to Korean barbecue joints — and its young, well-travelled diners treat new cuisines as a weekend plan, not a risk. Singapore, meanwhile, has deep culinary ties to India: a large Indian diaspora, generations of spice trade, and food cultures that already overlap more than either side admits.

Zi char also fills a real gap. Bengaluru's Chinese-food landscape is dominated by Indo-Chinese staples — Manchurian, Schezwan, Hakka noodles. Zi char offers something adjacent but distinct: a wok-driven cuisine that prizes freshness and communal sharing over the familiar gravy playbook. For a city that lines up for new openings the way it lines up for filter coffee, a Michelin-selected zi char arrival is event dining.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora in Singapore, KEK is already a landmark — a place where Indian-Singaporean families eat alongside everyone else at Alexandra Village. Its arrival in Bengaluru closes a small cultural loop: a cuisine shaped in part by Singapore's Indian community coming home to an Indian city.

What's Next

The question now is whether Bengaluru embraces zi char the way it has embraced every other global cuisine that has knocked on its door. If the queues at Alexandra Village are any indication, Moonlight Hor Fun's wok hei may soon have a second home.
